central_node: Textile Manufacturing, Spinning Mechanics, Weaving Structure, and Sustainability

key_details: Raw cotton fibers are short and break easily
Spinning continuously draws out and twists loose fibers
Torsional twisting creates lateral friction that binds fibers into strong yarn
Tools: Spindle pencils and traditional charkhas
Warp: Stationary vertical threads stretched on a loom
Weft: Horizontal threads woven over and under warp threads at right angles
Creates a stable planar woven fabric grid
Championed by Mahatma Gandhi during freedom movement
Symbolized economic self-reliance (Atmanirbhar) and rural empowerment
Harvested from Changthangi goats in cold Ladakh mountains
Nomadic Changpa herders comb out soft undercoat fleece by hand
Reusing old garments into patchwork quilts (gudris)
Reduces textile landfill waste and conserves raw fibers
